coverage: Eligibility sequences in the purposive corpus. Axes have different count ranges. The title sequence excludes titles that fail the English-likely gate or lack an uploader attribution. The caption sequence removes two unavailable tracks, three non-English tracks, one additional concordance sample, five videos without eligible matched titles, and three singleton publisher records. The final matched matrix therefore uses 22 videos from 11 publishers; the larger matched keyword table uses 25 videos. These are research-sample filters, not population attrition rates.
duration: Observed durations in six focal uploader samples. Filled points are medians; whiskers span linear 25th–75th percentiles and are not confidence intervals; open diamonds are means. All indexed videos in these six samples have known durations. The official Bashar account and Divine Insights are distinct publishers with different sampled upload durations. Format composition is one plausible explanation and has not been independently annotated. The figure does not estimate complete-channel means or compare practitioner session lengths.
matched-similarity: Matched title and caption comparisons use the same 22 videos in 11 publishers, yielding 55 dependent off-diagonal channel pairs. Left: cosines from the same pinned model, applied to different text units; their rank correlation is 0.206. The negative part of the title-cosine axis contains observed values. Right: each omission removes one publisher and all 10 incident pairs, leaving 45 pairs among 10 publishers. The dashed line is the full-sample correlation. The omission range [-0.043, 0.379] is a descriptive influence range, not a confidence interval or a significance test.
sensitivity: Left: agreement of off-diagonal similarity rankings under specified methodological changes. The first intervention jointly masks names and genre words, so its effect cannot be attributed to names alone. Comparisons use different cohorts and interventions; these values are not model accuracy or uncertainty estimates. Removing outer 10% of caption words from each end changes the nearest neighbor of 4 of 13 publishers. Weighting chunks by their content WordPiece counts changes 2 of 13 nearest neighbors despite rank correlation 0.984. Both caption comparisons use the same 26 documents in 13 two-video publisher groups. Right: all 30 English pilot caption lengths, from 87 to 8588 word tokens; median 1097.5. The logarithmic horizontal axis accommodates unequal lengths. Chunked embedding avoids truncating every recording to its beginning, while equal-video aggregation avoids giving longer recordings greater publisher weight.
